mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 400 d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt OM656 engines range from £4,200 to £6,500 depending on condition. With specialist fitting, budget £4,600-£7,300 total. OM642.853/873 (E 350 d, 258 hp, 2016-2018): rebuilt £3,200-£4,800. OM656.929 (E 400 d, 340 hp, 2018-2023): rebuilt £4,200-£6,500. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM656 tandem pump failure in an E Class 400 d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Intermittent limp mode that clears on restart, turbo actuator issues, and P0299E6 boost pressure codes are the classic signs. In severe cases, loss of braking assistance can occur. Intermittent power loss or limp mode, clearing on engine restart. P0299E6 error code (boost pressure too low). Juddering or clunky gear changes on longer journeys. Oil in vacuum lines (diagnostic check required).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an E Class 350 d or 400 d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound. W213 E 350 d examples command £15,000-£25,000 used, while E 400 d examples command £25,000-£40,000, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt OM642 costs £3,200-£4,800 supply only. A quality rebuilt OM656 costs £4,200-£6,500 supply only. The OM656 is the most powerful diesel engine Mercedes ever produced for a series car. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than the depreciation on a newer car.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM642 oil cooler seals to fail on E 350 d models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The rubber seals harden with heat cycles and degrade over time, causing oil to leak into the engine Vee. This is the defining weakness of the OM642 V6 engine family. Seal failure typically occurs between 60,000-100,000 miles. Oil drips under the engine bay and a burning oil smell are the early warning signs. Oil cooler seal replacement at a specialist costs £700-£1,100. Later OM642 engines (2014+) have improved seals but can still fail.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM642 and OM656 engines in the E Class?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 is a 3.0-litre V6 diesel (2016-2018 E 350 d); the OM656 is a 3.0-litre straight-six diesel (2018-2023 E 400 d) - more powerful, more refined, and borrowed from the S-Class. OM642: V6 configuration, 258 hp, 620 Nm - proven but has oil cooler seal issues. OM656: straight-six configuration, 340 hp, 700 Nm - smoother, more powerful, but has tandem pump issues. The OM656 replaced the OM642 in the E-Class from 2018 onwards. Both are Euro 6 compliant with AdBlue emissions treatment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 400 d engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and 8,000-10,000 mile oil changes, OM656 engines regularly reach 200,000+ miles. Some examples have exceeded 100,000 miles with proper servicing. OM656 straight-six is a modern, efficient design with robust bottom end. Tandem pump replacement at 40k-80k miles is a known requirement for early examples. Camshaft and rocker inspection at 80k-100k miles is recommended. Short oil change intervals (8k miles) are critical for longevity.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 350 d / 400 d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 350 d and E 400 d badges represented Mercedes-Benz's flagship six-cylinder diesel offerings across the W213 E-Class generation. The E 350 d launched with the proven OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel in 2016, before being replaced in 2018 by the E 400 d - powered by the all-new OM656 3.0-litre straight-six diesel, a more powerful and refined engine borrowed from the S-Class.

milestones.description: **2016** - W213 E 350 d launched with OM642 V6 diesel, 190 kW (258 hp), 620 Nm
**2017** - Mercedes temporarily suspended E 350 d sales in Germany due to NOx emissions compliance issues
**2018** - E 400 d introduced, replacing the E 350 d with the new OM656 3.0-litre straight-six diesel
**2021** - W213 facelift; E 400 d continues with revised OM656.929, now rated at 243 kW (330 hp) in some markets
**2023** - W214 generation launched; E-Class six-cylinder diesel offerings move to new engine architecture

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 350 d / 400 d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The E Class 350 d and 400 d represent the pinnacle of Mercedes six-cylinder diesel engineering in the W213 generation. The OM642 V6 is a proven, mature design - but carries the infamous oil cooler seal failure that has plagued this engine family for years. The later OM656 straight-six is more powerful and refined, but introduces its own set of complex issues, particularly around the integrated oil/vacuum pump. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Failure - The E 350 d V6 Weakness
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler sits in the engine Vee and uses rubber seals that harden with heat cycles. When they fail, oil leaks into the Vee, runs down the block, and can eventually mix with coolant. The seals themselves cost as little as £5, but the labour is extensive - the intake manifold and numerous ancillaries must be removed to access them.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of intake manifold, replacement of cooler seals, clean oil residue, refill fluids

repairOptions.tier: Major - Oil Cooler Seals Plus Ancillaries
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seal replacement plus new turbo oil feed lines, injector seals, and intake gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles; addresses multiple OM642 leak points

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM642 with upgraded Viton oil cooler seals and new turbo lines
repairOptions.longevity: When oil has emulsified coolant or damaged bearings

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W213 E 350 d is worth £15,000-£25,000 depending on condition and mileage. Given the high residual value, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals and warranty is almost always justifiable if the rest of the car is sound.
problems.recommendation: If caught early with no oil-coolant emulsion, specialist seal replacement at £700-£1,100 is all you need. Once oil has blocked the turbo feed lines or emulsified coolant has damaged bearings, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals becomes the most cost-effective long-term solution. Don't ignore oil drips under the engine bay - that's the telltale sign.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes E Class 350 d engine prices

problems.h4: OM656 Tandem Oil/Vacuum Pump Failure - The E 400 d Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The oil pump and vacuum pump are integrated into a single tandem unit. The seal between the oil and vacuum sides can degrade, allowing oil into the vacuum system. This compromises turbo actuator vacuum, causing intermittent limp mode, and in severe cases, complete loss of braking assistance. Early production OM656 engines (pre-2020) are more susceptible. The vacuum pipes that actuate the turbo can also collapse due to heat exposure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspection of vacuum lines, replacement of collapsed turbo actuator hoses
repairOptions.longevity: Early stage; when intermittent limp mode first appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of oil/vacuum pump assembly - engine-out job on OM656
repairOptions.longevity: When pump seal has failed; engine out required as timing chain is at the rear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM656 with new pump and all associated components
repairOptions.longevity: When pump failure has caused catastrophic engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W213 E 400 d is worth £25,000-£40,000 depending on condition and mileage. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value, making a rebuilt engine with warranty the clear choice for a high-value E 400 d.
problems.recommendation: The tandem pump failure is a known design weakness on the OM656 - if your E 400 d experiences intermittent limp mode or a P0299E6 boost pressure code, get the vacuum system inspected promptly. A £250-£500 diagnosis and pipe replacement is far cheaper than the £1,800+ engine-out pump replacement. However, if the pump seal has already failed and oil has contaminated the vacuum system, the engine-out pump replacement is unavoidable. Given the £25,000+ value of most W213 E 400 d examples, this is a repair worth making.
problems.cta: -> Get OM656 Mercedes E Class 400 d tandem pump and turbo quotes

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Camshaft Wear - The OM656 Top-End Concern
problems.rootCause: Camshaft and rocker arm wear has been reported on OM654 and OM656 engines. The timing chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, making replacement an engine-out job. Extended oil change intervals and stop-start operation accelerate wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of camshafts, rocker arms and followers
Supply & fit of rebuilt OM656 with new valvetrain components
repairOptions.longevity: When wear has caused catastrophic engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W213 E 400 d £25,000-£40,000). At this vehicle value, £900-£1,600 for camshaft work is a relatively minor expense to protect a high-value asset.
problems.recommendation: Camshaft and rocker wear is a known issue on higher-mileage OM656 engines. Regular oil changes (8,000-10,000 miles) with the correct specification oil are critical to prevent premature wear. If you hear unusual top-end noise from your E 400 d, have it inspected promptly - early intervention can prevent a £4,200+ engine replacement.
